top_story.headline: Rep. Dan Crenshaw still has no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 67 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: It is the one sitting member the Deadline Watch flags as missing a CY2025 annual report past every extension.
paragraphs: Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2) filed for an extension on 6/4/2026. His final extension date was 8/13/2026, and no calendar-year 2025 annual financial disclosure appears in the Clerk of the House index or Senate eFD. That leaves the report 67 days overdue.
The Deadline Watch notes that a filing under an unexpected spelling of a name can look like a missing one, so the absence reflects the indexes checked and not a confirmed failure to file.

Separately, seven confirmed officials still lack a posted certification of ethics-agreement compliance, the longest outstanding being Michelle White Bowman, Governor and Vice Chairman for Supervision of the Federal Reserve System Board of Governors, at 412 days past due. The details are in the Ethics Agreement Tracker below.

sections.headline: No New Ethics Filings Reported
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics filing window (October 16–19) contained three filings that had been previously reported, with no new divestitures, terminations, or disclosures requiring attention this period.

sections.headline: No new House or Senate disclosures in the window
paragraphs: The input held no House or Senate financial disclosures filed from 2026-10-16 onward that earlier editions had not already reported. No periodic transaction reports were parsed.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.

footer.sources: OGE ethics-filing search; DOJ FARA e-file system; LDA API (lda.gov); Clerk of the House financial disclosures; Senate eFD.
footer.known_gaps: The LDA API (lda.gov) returned HTTP 503, so the LDA section is empty and the lobbying-based extras (Industries to Watch for prediction markets, crypto and digital assets, artificial intelligence and defense tech, and Pardon Lobbying) could not be checked; their 'no new filings' results are not confirmed. The OGE section reported no new filings, with three previously reported filings in the window. The Deadline Watch notes that a name-spelling mismatch can make a filed disclosure look missing.
